chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of A'yan, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
If a man becomes certain that he has added to his obligatory salat (prayer), he does not count it, and he begins his salat anew, if he has indeed become certain with certainty.

key_terms.اسْتَقْبَلَ صَلَاتَهُ: he restarts his salat (prayer) from the beginning
key_terms.زَادَ: added an extra act or part
key_terms.لَمْ يَعْتَدَّ بِهَا: he does not regard it as valid or count it

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he becomes certain that he added something to his obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who becomes certain that he has made an addition in his obligatory salat (prayer). In such a case, the prayer is not to be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning when the certainty is definite.
